name: Ralph terminal (any outcome) → coordinator walker wake-up
description:
ADR-044 Slice 3 — when a Ralph (dev-via-test-execute) loop terminates for any reason, wake up the coordinator walker to decide the next move. Fires on outcome IN [success, failed, truncated, cancelled] — covers all four terminal classes per Slice 2 reviewer R1. The walker reads Ralph's terminal via read_loop_result + run-entity execution state via query_entity, computes 'what next' (dispatch next task, ask_user about a failure/clarification, or respond_direct when all tasks complete).

Rules 04a/04b (Slice 2) already stamped dev_via_test.execute.task_completed (success+pass) or .task_failed (any non-success) on the run entity — the walker reads those markers + the plan to compute progress. For Ralph terminals with outcome=success but decide(needs_clarification) — no marker is stamped by 04a/04b; the walker reads Ralph's terminal via read_loop_result and routes to ask_user with Ralph's reason.

Each Ralph instance is a new entity, so this rule fires once per Ralph (no Pattern A presence-marker needed — the entity is fresh, not re-evaluated).

on_enter.subject: agent.task.coordinator
on_enter.prompt:
DEV-VIA-TEST WALKER (post-Ralph) — Ralph at loop $entity.instance just terminated. Decide the next move.

Your run entity ID is $entity.triple.lineage.run-loop-entity-id.

Step 1 — read Ralph's terminal:
  read_loop_result(loop_id="$entity.instance") returns Ralph's decide(action, reason).
  Possible actions:
  - measured → Ralph converged. Run entity already has dev_via_test.execute.task_completed=<this-ralph-id> stamped (rule 04a). Walker advances.
  - needs_clarification → Ralph escalated. NO completion stamp. Walker routes to ask_user with Ralph's reason verbatim.
  - (no decide / outcome=failed|truncated|cancelled) → Ralph crashed or max-iter. Run entity has dev_via_test.execute.task_failed=<this-ralph-id> stamped (rule 04b). Walker routes to ask_user with Ralph's stderr_tail (read it from Ralph's loop entity via query_entity).

Step 2 — read run-entity state:
  query_entity(entity_id="$entity.triple.lineage.run-loop-entity-id") returns ALL run-entity triples including:
  - plan.task.<id>.* for every task (the plan, immutable)
  - dev_via_test.execute.task_completed (multi-valued: one per successfully-converged Ralph)
  - dev_via_test.execute.task_failed (multi-valued: one per loop-failed Ralph)

Step 3 — compute next move:
  Effective per-task status = ready, EXCEPT:
  - In task_completed list → done (skip)
  - In task_failed list → blocked (skip; the failure already drove an ask_user)
  Find the lowest-position task that's still ready. If found, dispatch.

Step 4 — decide:
  - Next ready task exists AND Ralph just converged → decide(action="dev_via_test", subtopics=["<task-id>"]). Scratchpad your reasoning first.
  - All tasks done (no ready remaining) → decide(action="dev_via_test_finalize", reason="<2-3 sentence pre-CBG rollup of what shipped; cite the integration_test_command>"). Rule 06 dispatches CBG to run the integration test; rules 07a/07b route CBG's approve/reject back to you for the FINAL user-facing reply.
  - Ralph escalated (needs_clarification) → decide(action="ask_user", reason="<quote Ralph's reason; ask user to amend the spec, abandon the task, or split it>").
  - Ralph loop-failed → decide(action="ask_user", reason="task <id> stuck — last error: <stderr_tail snippet>. Continue with a hint, abandon the task, or kill the chain?").

See your persona's 30-plan-walking.md fragment for the full walker contract.

metadata.phase: ADR-044 Slice 3 — walker wake-up after Ralph
metadata.no_pattern_a_note: Unlike autoresearch rule 05 (iteration dispatch) which uses Pattern A presence-marker on a recurring entity, this rule fires on per-Ralph entity transitions. Each Ralph is a NEW loop entity, so conditions evaluate fresh on each terminal — no monotonic-condition trap, no remove-then-add cycle needed.
metadata.slice_4_handoff: When Slice 4 lands CBG, this rule's prompt step 4 'all tasks done' branch will be replaced — instead of decide(respond_direct) directly, the walker will decide(action=dev_via_test_cbg) (or similar) routing to a CBG-dispatch rule. The CBG-approval rule then wakes a final coordinator for respond_direct.
